content:
Aiyana Brooks-Tan
Dublin, Ireland
aiyana.brookstan@example.com | +353 55 555 0404

Dear Verdane Care Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience team. I have hands-on experience building web applications with React and TypeScript, and I am especially interested in making digital services accessible and straightforward for the people who rely on them.

During my Software Development Internship at Harbourline Media, I worked on its React news site, resolving accessibility audit issues across more than 20 components, including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels. I also built a reusable, keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly image gallery, documented it with Storybook, and wrote unit tests using Jest and React Testing Library.

My final-year project, Tidewatch, gave me experience building across the stack: I developed a React and TypeScript frontend, a Node.js/Express API, and PostgreSQL storage for user favourites. I tested the app with NVDA and VoiceOver, and it achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100. The project received a First Class grade. I have also built a booking website with Next.js and Tailwind CSS.

Verdane Care’s focus on patient experience, accessibility and “Privacy by default” appeals to me. I would value the opportunity to contribute my frontend and project experience to software that helps patients manage appointments and follow-up care. My portfolio is available at aiyana-bt.example.com.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Patient Experience team.

Yours sincerely,
Aiyana Brooks-Tan

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, concise and professional cover letter with a strong evidence-based narrative. It gives specific examples from the Harbourline Media internship and Tidewatch, including the number of affected components, accessibility techniques, testing tools, technologies and project outcome. The tone is appropriate for a healthcare technology company and the letter avoids unsupported claims. The main content limitation is that it does not mention relevant teaching or mentoring experience, Git/GitHub, or the candidate’s specific accessibility knowledge such as WCAG 2.1. It also presents Tidewatch as broad full-stack experience without explicitly clarifying that it was an academic project, which could create an overly senior impression when read against the requirement for 2+ years of professional experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The cover letter is highly parseable: it uses standard headings-free prose, conventional paragraphs, plain text contact details, and the exact target job title. It includes valuable ATS terms such as React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels, Storybook, Jest, React Testing Library, Next.js and Tailwind CSS. AI screening probability is good because the evidence is concrete and closely related to the role. It could be improved by naturally adding supported terms from the candidate material: Git/GitHub, WCAG 2.1, and teaching or mentoring. Do not add end-to-end testing, OWASP, GDPR, NestJS, Docker, AWS, or healthcare-data experience because these are not supported by the original candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role’s React/TypeScript frontend work, Node.js/Express and PostgreSQL project experience, accessibility focus, automated unit testing, Storybook, Next.js, and the company’s patient-focused mission. The Tidewatch project and the yoga booking site provide relevant user-facing and wellness-related evidence. The candidate’s accessibility experience is particularly persuasive for Verdane Care’s WCAG-focused patient experience team. However, the candidate’s material does not establish 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience; Tidewatch is an academic project, and the professional roles shown are shorter or do not clearly cover the full requirement. The candidate also lacks evidence of end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, GDPR or health-data privacy, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, analytics/A-B testing, and regulated healthcare experience. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be fixed by rewriting. The stated Dublin location and remote preference may also conflict with the advertised remote-work countries, which are Austria, Germany, Croatia and Slovenia, or with hybrid work in Graz.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL/TRUTHFULNESS AND ALIGNMENT
1. In the paragraph beginning “My final-year project, Tidewatch,” change “My final-year project, Tidewatch, gave me experience building across the stack” to “My final-year project, Tidewatch, gave me academic project experience building across the stack.” This preserves the strong full-stack evidence while clearly distinguishing it from professional experience.

2. In the Harbourline Media paragraph, after “React Testing Library,” add the supported Git-based workflow evidence: “I used Git/GitHub in my development work.” Keep this wording limited to Git/GitHub; do not claim a specific branching, code-review or CI workflow that is not documented.

3. In the same Harbourline Media paragraph, change “including keyboard navigation, colour contrast and ARIA labels” to “including keyboard navigation, colour contrast, ARIA labels and WCAG 2.1 accessibility considerations.” This uses a supported candidate skill and better matches the job’s accessibility terminology. Do not change WCAG 2.1 to WCAG 2.2, because the original information supports only WCAG 2.1.

RELEVANT MINOR ENHANCEMENT
4. In the paragraph describing Tidewatch, add a final sentence before “I have also built a booking website...” stating: “As a teaching assistant in a first-year web development lab, I also supported approximately 30 students during one semester.” This truthfully highlights mentoring experience relevant to the role without overstating it.

5. In the final paragraph before the closing, replace “I would value the opportunity to contribute my frontend and project experience to software that helps patients manage appointments and follow-up care” with “I would value the opportunity to contribute my frontend experience, accessibility work and full-stack academic project experience to software that helps patients manage appointments and follow-up care.” This is more precise about the level and source of the candidate’s experience.
